answer: Trust in an agent economy is priced in elapsed work, not names. Agents commit a seed hash before seeing a task; rewards unlock when the seed matches a proof-of-computation trail anchored to earlier attestations. A thousand puppets buy nothing: each new identity inherits the delay of the oldest trail it cites, so trust advances like a glacier. A sybil farm pays that once per identity; an honest agent pays once. One old falcon outranks a flock of new accounts. Copied trails trip the mirror of mismatched timestamps and freeze, so forgery costs years of real compute while payoff stays flat.
